author: Cinna Davis (OpenAI Codex assisted)
statement: For raw charged pieces with polynomial shift weights of degree at most b, any linear extraction annihilating q-degrees below d has length support threshold e=d-b and exact structural rank given by a minimum threshold cover. Positive limiting e/h forces leading label-capacity loss and a quantified necessary grade increase; this is not a SAT bound. At the maximum effective degree 2h, a raw charged piece attains the rank-one mask via an explicit scalar output on the all-ones labels. At degree 2h-1, an outer-shift raw piece realizes a nonsingular scalar two-label pairing. One degree lower, the all-ones pair at the same shift is a weighted number operator with simple spectrum on the grade-h output space, so scalar invariant subspaces have dimension at most one. A concrete adjacent-shift grade-four collision shows that simple spectrum does not extend unchanged. At that finite adjacent-shift example, all 25 label-pair operators act scalarly on the two-dimensional output space with label rank three. At the adjacent shift the same all-ones operator has simple spectrum for every h>=5, limiting scalar invariant output subspaces to dimension one. Preserving exp(kappa sqrt(h)-O(log h)) label capacity requires effective degree O(sqrt(h) log h), and that condition is sufficient for the unrestricted mask. A sign-variation argument and reflected-walk determinant prove weighted outer shifts cannot give a nonzero scalar on the full grade-h output space for this one all-ones label pair. Explicit high-shift weights give a full-label scalar pairing while removing the central |s|<h interval, but its label rank is exactly three for h>=3.
remaining_obligations: Independent review of the proof and asymptotics
Scalarization, output capacity and both crossing ranks remain open; arbitrary charge-dependent normalization is not covered
Relate any filter to full algorithmic costs before claiming a SAT improvement
